event_types.label: Planting reported
event_types.description: The tree was planted, or was found in, or moved to, a different spot.

event_types.label: Placed outside the orchard
event_types.description: The tree is meant to go outside the orchard, and its place is not yet known.

event_types.label: Death reported
event_types.description: The owner reported the tree dead. The notes say what is known about when and where.

event_types.label: Lost before planting
event_types.description: The tree died, or was judged too poor to plant, while it was still in its pot. It was never in the ground here.

event_types.label: Lost after planting
event_types.description: A planted tree died. Also mark the plant and its planting dead, and say in the notes when it was last seen alive and what the damage looked like.

event_types.label: Identified
event_types.description: The cultivar of an unidentified tree was worked out. The notes give the evidence.

event_types.label: Bud swell
event_types.description: The buds are visibly swelling in late winter or early spring.

event_types.label: Bud break
event_types.description: The buds have opened and the first green shows (green tip on apples and pears).

event_types.label: Leaf out
event_types.description: About half of the leaf buds have opened.

event_types.label: First bloom
event_types.description: The first flowers are open.

event_types.label: Full bloom
event_types.description: About 80 percent of the flowers are open.

event_types.label: Petal fall
event_types.description: Most of the petals have fallen.

event_types.label: Fruit set
event_types.description: Small fruit are visibly set and growing.

event_types.label: First harvest
event_types.description: The first ripe fruit is picked.

event_types.label: Fall color
event_types.description: About half of the leaves have changed color.

event_types.label: Leaf drop
event_types.description: About half of the leaves have fallen.

event_types.label: Survival check
event_types.description: A check on whether the tree is alive, usually in spring after winter. The notes say alive, damaged (and where), or dead.

event_types.label: Winter injury
event_types.description: Dieback, split bark, or dead buds after winter. The notes say how much and where.

event_types.label: Frost damage
event_types.description: Frost damage to blossoms, young fruit, or new growth. The notes give the night's low if known and how much was hurt.

event_types.label: Pest or disease
event_types.description: A pest, canker, rot, or other disease seen on the tree. The notes say what it is and how bad.

event_types.label: Bloom noted
event_types.description: A note about the blossoms (color, size, scent) that helps identify the tree.

event_types.label: Fruit noted
event_types.description: A note about the fruit (size, color, flavor, yield, keeping) for identification and to judge quality.

event_types.label: Bark noted
event_types.description: A note about the bark (color, texture, peeling) that helps identify the tree.

event_types.label: Leaf noted
event_types.description: A note about the leaves (shape, size, color, glands) that helps identify the tree.

event_types.label: Habit noted
event_types.description: A note about the tree's size, shape, and vigor.

event_types.label: Other note
event_types.description: Any other observation worth keeping.
